before.description_1: There were good pieces of information on driving schools at SoDrive, but the message should have been more structured and prioritized. People should be able to scan through and understand what's in it for them, and how to proceed next easily. The wording should not be generic either.
before.description_2: As a result, I have written the text anew in such a way that each section of the page provides an answer to one specific visitor's question. In this way, my rewritten case study provides information about the driving school job opportunities in simple language and shows how their advantages will affect you in your decisions.

after.description_1: SoDrive is a driving school website built around helping learners understand lesson options, packages, the route to a licence and the next step toward starting lessons. The portfolio copy needed to describe that learner journey clearly rather than referring to job opportunities.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around practical driving-school information, package comparison, trust signals and clear trial-lesson or contact actions. The responsive layout keeps the same decision path easy to follow for learners on mobile and desktop.

before.description_1: Boekhoudsnel needed a clearer finance page because visitors had to understand the offer before making contact. The existing story needed stronger order, more specific wording, and fewer general lines. People comparing options needed quick context, visible next steps, and enough practical detail to decide whether to continue. Before contact mattered.
before.description_2: I rebuilt the page around clearer sections, direct English copy, and practical WordPress content blocks. The structure shows what the work involves, why it matters, and how visitors can respond. Stronger scanning, calmer wording, and focused contact routes help people compare the project and make decisions with confidence. It mattered.

after.description_1: Boekhoudsnel presents bookkeeping support for entrepreneurs who want administrative work explained in practical terms. The website needed to make the service, expected support and route to contact understandable without relying on broad finance language.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress content around the bookkeeping proposition, practical questions and a clear enquiry route. The linked URL stored in ACF was malformed and could not be independently verified, so I removed that invalid value instead of replacing it with an unverified domain.

before.description_1: Regarding the energy page of Voltworks, there was a need to avoid any delay in action when the visitor was considering enquiring. The visitor would already be making comparisons, so there was a need to explain clearly what the company could do, the details involved, and what the next step was.
before.description_2: I have developed a streamlined approach to navigating the site through more concise headers and content fields in WordPress, as well as the proper wording for their projects. The design will provide better representation for Voltworks, while the visitor will be able to browse their work, discern its value, and proceed towards contacting them.

after.description_1: Voltworks presents energy solutions through a service-focused website where visitors need to understand the available technical options before requesting advice or a quotation. The content therefore needed to make the offer concrete instead of using generic language about enquiries.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around the main energy services, supporting project information and clear contact or quotation actions. Technical detail remains available, but the first layer helps visitors identify the relevant solution and move toward a conversation.

before.description_1: Jouwgroenteboer needed a clearer ecommerce page, so visitors could understand the offer before contacting or taking action. The existing story needed more structure, more precise wording and a clearer route forward for people comparing options online.
before.description_2: I restructured the site into logical sections using plain English and WordPress content blocks. The new flow explains the offer, why it matters and what visitors can do next. Better scanning, clearer language and a defined contact path help people evaluate the project with confidence.

after.description_1: Jouwgroenteboer is an ecommerce experience for ordering fresh fruit and vegetables online. The website needed to make categories, products, delivery information and the shopping route easy to understand so customers can move from browsing to ordering without unnecessary friction.
after.description_2: I organised the WooCommerce journey around product discovery, clear category structure and direct cart actions. Supporting information stays close to the shopping flow, while the responsive layout keeps browsing and checkout practical on smaller screens.

before.description_1: Kervana needed the call to action and service offer to be clear within a few seconds. The page had to explain what the installation service includes, who it is for and why visitors should contact the business.
before.description_2: I improved the readability of the installation story with a stronger opening, clearer service sections and practical information that supports the next step. The WordPress layout makes the page easy to scan, while the copy gives visitors enough context to act confidently.

after.description_1: Kervana brings installation services such as climate, heating and related technical solutions together in one WordPress presentation. The website needed to distinguish those services clearly and give visitors enough practical context before they request advice or a quotation.
after.description_2: I structured the content around the main installation routes, project or service proof and direct enquiry actions. Shorter sections make the technical offer easier to scan, while the responsive layout keeps contact and quotation options close to the relevant service.

before.description_1: Envolt needed an electrical services page with a clearer structure and stronger focus. Visitors had to understand the offer quickly, see the practical value and know how to take the next step. The copy also needed to sound more specific and less interchangeable.
before.description_2: I reorganised the page into clear sections that answer the most important visitor questions. The final WordPress page explains the electrical work in plain language, connects benefits to real decisions and keeps contact options visible, making the project easier to read and trust.

after.description_1: Envolt presents electrical and energy services through a focused business website. The portfolio copy needed to explain the actual technical offer and decision path instead of using a sentence accidentally stored in the URL field and generic wording about enquiries.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around the main electrical and energy services, supporting information and clear contact actions. The malformed ACF link was replaced with the project domain, and the content now describes the service journey rather than a generic page-improvement process.

before.description_1: The ozturkmotionpictures website required better wedding information because it was important for people to get the offer before they contacted the company. There was also a need to improve the narrative in terms of structure and wording. Comparing various alternatives meant that people would have to find out quickly what next step to take.
before.description_2: I rebuilt the page around clean sections, clear language, and practical WordPress content modules. The new structure helps visitors understand the project, see the value of the service, and find the next step without friction.

after.description_1: Ozturk Motion Pictures is a wedding-focused visual portfolio built around films, photography, couple stories and galleries. The website needed to let prospective couples understand the style of the work quickly and move naturally from viewing previous weddings to making contact.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress presentation around visual project browsing, concise service context and a clear enquiry route. Large imagery and galleries remain the main proof, while supporting copy helps couples understand what they can request without distracting from the portfolio.

before.description_1: Since the site failed to have accurate information on its pages, it became necessary that essential facts about the property be clearly visible right from the beginning. An effective introduction became important because it could assist in directing users into going through all the sections of the site easily while understanding the offer clearly.
before.description_2: The design for Odetra was improved, with the usage of better English language, but still keeping the content organized. The page contains a clear description of the real estate services provided, no distractions whatsoever, the page allows quick comparison by visitors, and works perfectly on WordPress across all devices.

after.description_1: Odetra presents international real-estate investment and project-development opportunities. The website needed to keep property and market information clear enough for visitors to understand the proposition before moving into company information or direct contact.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around projects, market context and the company proposition, with a clear route from evaluating opportunities to making an enquiry. The content hierarchy keeps property information central and avoids generic claims that could apply to any real-estate website.

before.description_1: It was necessary to narrow down the topics on which Marco Verhuurt could be discussed, since users cannot guess what kind of service the rental project provides. It required clear sections, specific language, and sufficient explanations to build trust without complicating the initial stage of contacting.
before.description_2: The design of the last page focused on clear language, balanced parts, and contact opportunities that come up once there is sufficient background information for the user. It is easier to follow what must be done next in the process of renting, which makes the page more convincing for Marco Verhuurt. Contact used to matter more.

after.description_1: Marco Verhuurt is a rental-focused website where visitors need to understand the available offer, practical conditions and availability before making an enquiry. The portfolio copy therefore needed to describe the rental journey directly instead of speaking generally about page clarity.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around the rental options, availability and the next contact step. Practical information appears before the enquiry point, giving visitors enough context to decide whether an available option fits their needs.

before.description_1: The biggest obstacle for Palmeroshop involved presenting the offer in a way that would be quickly understandable. This meant that the page needed to make clear what the offer included, who it served, and why contact should be initiated, without using generic phrases that could apply equally well to another site.
before.description_2: I simplified the beauty story by adding an impactful introduction, defining services in clear sections, and putting practical information close to action points. The WordPress layout enables fast browsing, both on desktop and mobile devices, making it easy for visitors to comprehend the offer and choose to connect with Palmeroshop. This made a lot of sense.

after.description_1: Palmero Shop is an ecommerce site for massage guns and recovery accessories. Product education, supporting articles, FAQs, delivery and return information all need to work together so customers understand the products before they decide to buy.
after.description_2: I structured the WooCommerce experience around product-led browsing, clear product explanations and a direct shopping route. Educational content supports the purchase decision without interrupting it, while store policies and FAQs remain easy to reach before checkout.

before.description_1: The Energy page for Solar Daktechnique entailed the removal of any sort of reservations before proceeding to inquire about anything. This visitor was likely comparing other firms, and therefore it was necessary to clarify what the firm had to offer and what steps followed thereafter. The use of general language would have caused confusion.
before.description_2: I have made the way simpler to move through shorter headings, more specific descriptions for projects, and also WordPress post information that is quite easy to maintain in the future. It not only enhances the presentation of Solar Daktechnique but also ensures that no visitor finds any difficulty browsing through the portfolio or contacting the company.

after.description_1: Solar Daktechnique presents solar panels, charging solutions and related electrical work through a technical energy-services website. Visitors needed to understand the available solutions and the company’s practical role before requesting a quotation or making contact.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress content around the main energy-service choices, supporting technical information and clear quotation routes. The first layer stays easy to scan, while deeper detail remains available for visitors who want to compare solutions before enquiring.

before.description_1: Neutralhome needed content that was easier on the eyes and would make it easy to compare the various services available to them. The page needed to describe the interior design work done, without making the content hard to read, and at the same time provide enough information so as to convince someone to contact the company.
before.description_2: I structured the page around what visitors need to understand first: the offer, the value, and the next step. Clearer paragraphs, concise wording, and focused WordPress delivery make the interior project easier to assess and more convincing for potential inquiries.

after.description_1: Netural Home combines sanitary products, floors, tiles and renovation projects with showroom advice. The website needed to work as an inspiration layer first, then help visitors translate what they see into a practical appointment or quotation.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around product and renovation categories, project inspiration and tailored showroom advice. Visitors can browse ideas, understand the available interior options and move naturally toward an appointment or quote without losing the visual focus.

before.description_1: Oxford Academy's content was supposed to be made more precise in order to avoid having visitors guessing about the offerings of the education project. What was needed was well-structured, clear content with appropriate wording that provided adequate information for building trust but did not make initial contact complicated.
before.description_2: I created a clearer page structure with simple language, balanced sections, and contact moments placed where visitors are ready to act. The result is an education website that is easier to follow and more convincing for prospective students or parents.

after.description_1: Oxford Academy brings tutoring, homework guidance, exam preparation, remedial support and school services together across its education offering. The website needed to help parents and students understand those options, locations and approach before choosing a trial lesson or signup route.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around the main education services, the academy’s step-by-step approach, teacher and review proof and clear registration actions. The structure keeps the different forms of support distinct while making the next step easy to find.

before.description_1: The website was in need for Marcosmontage due to certain issues. First of all, there should have been enough information provided about the offer regarding the exhibition. Secondly, there should have been enough detail provided about the contact information of the owner of the gallery and the place itself.
before.description_2: I worked on the page by eliminating any form of repetition and reorganizing the structure of the content in a more concise way. This WordPress site is able to present the proposal in its practical context and with a steady pace that makes it easy for visitors to find their motivation.

after.description_1: Marcos Montage is an installation-services website, not an exhibition or gallery project. The website needed to explain the practical technical work clearly and give prospective customers a direct route from the relevant service to quotation or contact.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress presentation around concise service information and visible enquiry actions. The corrected portfolio copy removes the unrelated gallery references and describes the actual installation-focused customer journey across desktop and mobile.

before.description_1: Homeplaza needed stronger page copy because important information about the interior offer was not clear enough at the start. Visitors needed a more engaging introduction, a better structure and a simple explanation of the service before deciding to contact the company.
before.description_2: I improved the clarity of the site with a stronger structure and more natural English. The service information is easier to scan, easier to compare and more consistent across the WordPress presentation, helping visitors understand the offer before taking action.

after.description_1: Home Plaza covers kitchens, bathrooms, floors, wall finishes, steel doors, custom cabinetry, stair renovation and complete home renovation. The website needed to make that broad interior offer browsable while connecting inspiration and showroom information to a practical project process.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around the main renovation categories, project steps and showroom proof. Visitors can move from exploring a specific part of the home to arranging an appointment or quotation, while the overall presentation still feels like one complete renovation proposition.

before.description_1: In the case of Brightlyn, the major difficulty was in ensuring that the offer on cybersecurity was clear enough for the potential customers in just a few seconds. The web page needed to be able to show what the offer entailed, which group would benefit from it, and why it makes sense to get in touch.
before.description_2: The process involved converting the story on cyber security into a simplified experience that had a stronger introduction and service blocks that were easier to understand, with relevant information close to where action needed to be taken. This was made possible because of the ease of navigating the website on mobile and desktops.

after.description_1: Brightlyn is a cybersecurity and regulatory consultancy whose services cover risk, resilience, DORA, NIS2 and assurance. The website needed to translate complex advisory subjects into clear service routes while showing the sectors and end-to-end approach behind the work.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress content around the main cybersecurity and compliance needs, sector context and direct consultation options. The structure makes technical regulation easier to scan without oversimplifying the expertise, helping business visitors identify the relevant advisory route.

before.description_1: YCO IT needed an offer that visitors could understand within a few seconds. The page had to explain the services, who they are for, and why someone should get in touch, without relying on broad phrases that could apply to almost any company.
before.description_2: I simplified the compliance story into a more linear page structure, with a stronger introduction, clearer service blocks, and specific information at the right action points. The website is easier to scan on desktop and mobile, helping visitors understand the offer and decide whether to contact YCO IT.

after.description_1: YCO IT focuses on risk management and compliance, including subjects such as ISAE, ISO 27001 and 27701, control concepts and security or compliance assessments. The website needed to make those specialist services understandable to organisations evaluating governance and assurance support.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around the main compliance and risk topics, practical assessment routes and clear contact points. Technical standards remain visible as proof of scope, while the page hierarchy helps visitors identify which service matches their organisation’s need.

before.description_1: DM Elektro already had useful information about electrical work, but the message needed clearer priorities and a calmer structure. Visitors had to recognise the benefits quickly, understand the service and see a straightforward next step. The copy also needed to feel specific rather than generic.
before.description_2: I rewrote and organised the information around the questions visitors are likely to have first. The page explains the electrical work, connects the benefits to practical decisions and keeps the contact route easy to find, using clear and direct language throughout.

after.description_1: DM Elektro presents electrical systems, lighting, solar solutions, batteries, heat pumps and maintenance through one technical-services website. The challenge was to keep the breadth of that offer understandable while giving visitors enough trust and service context before requesting a quote.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress content into distinct electrical and energy routes, supported by expertise and certification information. Clear quotation and contact actions stay close to the relevant service, making it easier to move from a technical need to a concrete enquiry.

before.description_1: Fixfinder required better clarity for their repair service webpage since the prospect would have to comprehend the offer before contacting. The current story required greater order and more precise language. It had to convey information to help prospects make an informed decision on what to do next. Contact was important before making any move.
before.description_2: I restructured the page with clearer sections, plain English copy, and relevant WordPress content blocks. The new flow explains the service, why it matters, and how visitors can take the next step. Scannable content and clearer contact routes make the page easier to compare and act on.

after.description_1: Fixfinder helps motorists start with their vehicle and then find support for maintenance, repairs, tyres, keys, towing, damage or cleaning. The website needed to make that service-selection process simple enough that visitors can move from a problem to a relevant partner garage without guessing.
after.description_2: I structured the experience around entering the vehicle, choosing the required service and continuing toward an appropriate repair provider. Supporting explanations clarify the available categories while keeping the main task—finding the right automotive help—central on desktop and mobile.

before.description_1: The information found on the website was quite helpful for language-related queries. However, the tone used was very high-sounding and prioritization was not very clear in the text. The readers should be given a clear picture about the website and what they can get out of it just by having a glance.
before.description_2: In the end, there is a better website that does not just inform others about what your language service can do for you, but also gives answers that would be easy for any visitor to understand. I have organized the text in such a way that it provides answers to the questions asked by the visitor.

after.description_1: VoiceLinq provides interpreting and translation services with a network covering more than 50 languages and sectors such as legal, medical and business communication. The website needed to separate service requests from the route for interpreters who want to join the network.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around interpreting, translation and the two primary user journeys: requesting language support and becoming an interpreter. Clear service context and direct actions keep the broad language offer practical instead of abstract.

before.description_1: There was need for QuickTemp to provide answers to practical questions raised by their site visitors much faster. The job offer must be clearly explained with relevant details, context, and a way of contacting them. If not, the site might lose its focus hence appearing generic; it made quick judgment possible before any contact.
before.description_2: This is how I improved the page by getting rid of redundant parts, arranging the info properly, and making each block more scannable. This WordPress version of the recruiting pitch delivers all the information in a realistic setting, allowing people to see why it makes sense to keep on reading.

after.description_1: QuickTemp connects candidates and employers across sectors including hospitality, production, logistics and horticulture. The website needed to keep job discovery and flexible staffing enquiries separate while using the same sector expertise to support both audiences.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress experience around vacancies and candidate action on one side, and employer staffing needs on the other. Clear sector routes, practical information and direct contact actions help each audience move forward without sorting through the other journey.

before.description_1: There were many reasons why a clearer website was needed by VC Het Wonder for their health care project. Visitors had to be able to read the message and make their contact very quickly. The story that was there already lacked structure and clear wording. There was need for better and easy scanning information when writing about a health care organization.
before.description_2: My method of approaching Vchetwonder involved the use of a cleaner design through the application of WordPress and microcopy to make VC Het Wonder have more of a particular feel that can be easily navigated by those who are interested in viewing the projects.

after.description_1: VC Het Wonder is a healthcare website focused on maternity care around pregnancy, birth and the postnatal period. The portfolio copy needed to describe that care journey calmly and clearly rather than using generic language about a healthcare organisation.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress presentation around care information, locations and contact, using a calm hierarchy that helps expectant parents find the relevant stage of care. The public project site could not be fully fetched during verification, so I kept the corrected claims limited to the live WordPress project data.

before.description_1: However, prior to this change, the Starkeuken web pages required more focused information regarding the kitchen specifics as they were not apparent at first sight for some visitors. In addition, the site had to have an appealing opening statement, proper navigation and simple wording describing the deal before they contacted the company.
before.description_2: I refined the site by giving it more structure, cleaner English writing, and a more cohesive path through the introduction and contact form. This page provides a clean and concise overview of the kitchen services, making it easier for visitors to make comparisons and maintaining consistency throughout the WordPress layout on any device size.

after.description_1: Starkeuken presents fitted kitchens and related interior products such as appliances, worktops and tiles, with additional bathroom and sanitary options across its locations. The website needed to turn that broad showroom offer into a clear route from inspiration to advice.
after.description_2: I organised the WordPress experience around the main kitchen and interior categories, practical product information and location or contact routes. Visitors can compare options, understand the range and move toward showroom advice without the content feeling like generic kitchen marketing.

before.description_1: WordPress sites have the ability to accumulate large amounts of images very rapidly, leading to difficulties in maintaining an overview of all the images in use. This may cause users to overlook the availability of images, the places where they are used, or other pending tasks.
before.description_2: ModernImage provides an organized view of images for the user. It enables the user to locate his or her WordPress images easily. It provides better management of images. Users can control images through this plug-in effectively.

after.description_1: Modern Image Manager is a WordPress media-management plugin for reviewing image metadata, importing and exporting updates, scanning where images are used and creating controlled media ZIP exports. The workflow needed to support bulk maintenance without weakening validation or file-handling safety.
after.description_2: I built the admin workflow around metadata review, usage scanning, CSV-based updates and controlled export actions. Capability checks, validation and safer file boundaries keep large media tasks manageable while giving administrators a clearer overview of the library.

before.description_1: Wehear4u needed project content that was easier to read and more useful for quick comparison. The page had to explain the healthcare work in clear, accessible language, while giving visitors enough context to understand the service, trust the presentation, and decide whether to get in touch.
before.description_2: I structured the page around what visitors need to know first: the offer, the benefit, and the next step. Short sections, clearer wording, and focused WordPress delivery make the healthcare project easier to assess. The page now feels more specific, practical, and ready for inquiries.

after.description_1: WeHear4U is a healthcare project where visitors need calm, accessible information about care and treatment before deciding to make contact. The portfolio copy needed to reflect that patient-facing journey rather than describe generic improvements to a healthcare page.
after.description_2: I structured the WordPress presentation around clear care information, a calm reading hierarchy and visible contact options. The public project site presented a verification challenge during the audit, so the corrected wording stays within the scope confirmed by the live WordPress project data.
